- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 3–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (≥10% from prior high), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak for next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.8) and price is trending down, model often underestimates drop; add 1–2% downward bias to forecast if sentiment >0.8 and price >80.
- Model frequently overreacts to sentiment spikes; if sentiment rises sharply (e.g., from 0.2 to 0.8 in 3 days), reduce forecast by 2–4% to avoid overcorrection.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window; apply 1–3% downward adjustment for first 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or declining.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.4–0.8) and price is volatile, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply 1–2% downward adjustment for 3–5 days after sentiment stabilizes below 0.6.
